title: Unused Termination Share by Contract Term
content:
# Unused Termination Share by Contract Term

Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda — share schedule for terminations after a lienholder payoff report. The unused termination share of a Kessler GAP waiver depends on the term of the installment contract the waiver is attached to:

| Contract term | Unused termination share |
|---|---|
| 72 months or longer | Whole calendar months from the loan payoff date to the expiration date, divided by the term months |
| 48 months or shorter | Sum-of-the-digits share: unused whole months times (unused whole months plus one), divided by term months times (term months plus one) |
| 49 to 71 months | Calendar-day share: calendar days from the loan payoff date to the expiration date, divided by calendar days from the sale date to the expiration date |

The share is applied to the price amount the termination refund is figured from, and that product is rounded half up to the cent.

**Counting unused whole months.** Whole calendar months run from the loan payoff date the lienholder reported to the expiration date; a whole calendar month counts each time the start date's day of the month is reached, an end date on an earlier day of the month does not complete the month, and there is no month-end adjustment.

**Illustrations (hypothetical figures, price 681.00).**

- 48-month contract, 36 unused whole months: 36 times 37 is 1,332; 48 times 49 is 2,352; 681.00 times 1,332 divided by 2,352 is 385.6684..., rounded to 385.67.
- 84-month contract, 45 unused whole months: 681.00 times 45 divided by 84 is 364.8214..., rounded to 364.82.
- 60-month contract, 1,200 of 1,826 calendar days unused: 681.00 times 1,200 divided by 1,826 is 447.5356..., rounded to 447.54.

**Boundaries.** A 72-month contract takes whole months; a 71-month contract takes calendar days. A 48-month contract takes the sum of the digits; a 49-month contract takes calendar days.
